uncited: It differs from [Reference-free Image Quality Metrics](15295-reference-free-image-quality-metrics.md) by requiring ground-truth subjective data, and from [Target-Focused Quantitative Evaluation](18844-target-focused-quantitative-evaluation.md) by focusing on the statistical relationship between predicted and perceived quality rather than pixel-wise fidelity.
- Vectors $MOS$ and $MOS_p$ of size $N$, containing floating-point values.
where $\overline{MOS}$ and $\overline{MOS_p}$ are the means of the respective vectors.
An outlier is typically defined as a prediction error exceeding a threshold (e.g., $k$ standard deviations) from the mean error.
The OR is the fraction of samples classified as outliers.
This involves ranking the values in $MOS$ and $MOS_p$ and computing the Pearson correlation on the ranks.
- Division by zero in PCC if the variance of $MOS$ or $MOS_p$ is zero.
- Degenerate input where all predicted scores are identical.

- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ for PCC, SROCC, and RMSE, where $N$ is the number of samples. $O(N \log N)$ for SROCC due to sorting. $O(N)$ for NMI if histograms are precomputed, otherwise dependent on binning.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ to store the score vectors.
PCC and SROCC are standard for linear and monotonic relationships.
- **When to use:** When validating new objective metrics against human perception.
- **When not to use:** When no subjective data is available (use Reference-free metrics).
